# Lisbon 5-Day Slow-Travel Itinerary

A relaxed Lisbon plan for 2 adults, built around **one major activity per day**, late starts, museum time, local food, and easy walking. Budget target stays within **€1,800 total** excluding flights.

## Day-by-Day Plan and Cost Split

| Day | Plan | Estimated cost for 2 | Transit tip | Rainy-day backup |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Jun 10 | Baixa + Chiado walking, lunch, sunset miradouro | €250 | Use the **Metro** to Baixa-Chiado; walk or tram short hops only | Museu Nacional do Azulejo |
| Jun 11 | **National Tile Museum** as the main activity | €285 | Taxi/Uber is simplest; public transit works but is slower | Extend with café time in Alfama |
| Jun 12 | Belém food-and-museum day, relaxed afternoon | €320 | Go by tram/bus early afternoon; avoid peak lunch rush | MAAT or Coach Museum |
| Jun 13 | **Calouste Gulbenkian Museum** and garden time | €260 | Metro to São Sebastião is efficient | Indoor café + museum shop browsing |
| Jun 14 | Alfama stroll, market lunch, easy departure day | €225 | Use tram/Metro plus a short taxi if carrying luggage | Fado museum or indoor tasting stop |

## Daily Itinerary

### Day 1: Arrival, Baixa, and Chiado
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Late morning:** Check in, settle in, then do a gentle walk through Baixa and Chiado.
- **Major activity:** Keep it light today: architecture, viewpoints, and a long lunch rather than a museum marathon.
- **Relaxed afternoon:** Sit-down coffee and pastry break near Praça do Comércio or Rua Garrett.
- **Food:** Try bifana, bacalhau, and a first pastel de nata stop.
- **Transit tip:** Use the Metro from the airport or train station, then walk; Lisbon’s center is best on foot.

### Day 2: National Tile Museum
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Late morning:** Start with a slow breakfast, then head to the museum after the rush.
- **Major activity:** Spend 2–3 hours at the **National Tile Museum** for a focused museum day.
- **Relaxed afternoon:** Return to your neighborhood for a long lunch and downtime.
- **Food:** Choose a traditional tascas-style lunch with grilled fish or arroz de marisco.
- **Transit tip:** A taxi or ride-hail is the smoothest option; it saves energy for the museum visit.

### Day 3: Belém Food and Culture
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- **Late morning:** Head to Belém after breakfast and keep the morning unhurried.
- **Major activity:** Make **one** anchor stop here: either the Jerónimos area or a museum visit, not both at full pace.
- **Relaxed afternoon:** Spend the rest of the day wandering, eating, and sitting by the river.
- **Food:** Pastéis de Belém, codfish cakes, and a riverfront snack break.
- **Transit tip:** Tram/bus works well, but a taxi is worth it if you want to conserve walking energy.

### Day 4: Calouste Gulbenkian Museum
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/book.svg
- **Late morning:** Go to the museum after a slow start and coffee.
- **Major activity:** Visit the **Calouste Gulbenkian Museum** and keep the visit unhurried.
- **Relaxed afternoon:** Enjoy the gardens or a nearby café, then rest before dinner.
- **Food:** Pick a modern Portuguese lunch; this is a good day for a calm, sit-down meal.
- **Transit tip:** Metro to São Sebastião is efficient and avoids traffic.

### Day 5: Alfama, Market Lunch, and Departure Buffer
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg
- **Late morning:** Do a final walking loop through Alfama’s lanes and viewpoints.
- **Major activity:** Keep this as a flexible heritage-and-neighborhood day, not a packed sightseeing day.
- **Relaxed afternoon:** Leave a wide buffer for packing, luggage, and a final meal.
- **Food:** Try a last seafood lunch or petiscos before heading out.
- **Transit tip:** Use a short taxi if needed; cobblestones and luggage are not a great mix.

## Budget Fit for 2 Adults

| Category | Estimated total | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Accommodation | €750 | Comfortable mid-range stay for 4 nights |
| Food and drinks | €520 | Breakfasts, lunches, dinners, coffee, pastries |
| Local transit | €90 | Metro, tram, and a few taxis/Ubers |
| Museums and entry | €220 | Main museum tickets and minor entries |
| Buffer and extras | €220 | Snacks, water, small shopping, contingency |
| Total | **€1,800** | Matches your cap |

## Rainy-Day Backup Options

- **Best museum swap:** National Tile Museum or Calouste Gulbenkian Museum
- **Best indoor food plan:** Long café lunch, pastry tasting, and covered-market browsing
- **Best low-effort fallback:** Taxi between neighborhoods, then keep the rest of the day indoors
- **Best flexible add-on:** Fado performance or a second museum if weather is poor
